str1: Five skills adapted from a World Health Organization guide, breathing exercises (4-6, box, 4-7-8) and a free illustrated guide with audio exercises.
str2: Five skills that take a few minutes a day, adapted from the illustrated guide the World Health Organization wrote for everyone, plus a breathing exercise.
str5: Slowing your breathing helps your body calm down. Sit somewhere comfortable and let your shoulders drop. Breathe in through your nose as the circle grows and breathe out slowly as it shrinks. When the edge of the circle turns gold, hold your breath.
str9: Breathe in for 4 seconds and out for 6. No holding. Keep going for as long as you like.

str24: These skills are not meant to make stress disappear completely. The aim is to stay grounded even when difficult feelings are there, and to be able to turn back to what matters to you.
str26: When emotions come like a storm, it is like dropping anchor until the storm passes.
str28: Quietly notice what you are thinking and feeling right now.
str30: Press your feet into the floor, straighten your back, breathe out slowly and stretch your shoulders.
str32: Notice, one by one, the things you can see, hear and touch around you. Then go back to what you were doing.
str34: Difficult thoughts can catch us like a fishing hook and pull us away from the life we are living right now.
str35: Notice that a thought has hooked you.
str37: Say to yourself: “I’m noticing a difficult thought.”
str39: Bring your attention back to what you are doing and to the people around you.
str41: We cannot always change our circumstances, but we can choose the kind of person we want to be. What matters to you: being patient, kind, helpful?
str43: Choose a small, doable step that shows this value, such as calling a friend or helping a neighbour.
str45: Treat yourself the way you would treat a friend who is going through a hard time.
str47: Gently place a hand on your chest and feel its warmth.
str49: “This is really hard. I am not alone in feeling this way.”
str51: Fighting a difficult feeling often makes it bigger. Try carrying it with you for a while instead.
str53: Where in your body do you feel the emotion? If it were an object, what would its shape, colour and temperature be?
str55: Breathe out slowly around that area and make room for it. Feelings come and go.
str56: How do you do a breathing exercise when you are stressed?
str57: Sit somewhere comfortable and let your shoulders drop. Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds and out slowly over 6 seconds. One round takes 10 seconds; 6 rounds take about 1 minute. Slowing your breathing helps your body calm down.
str58: How do you do box breathing and 4-7-8 breathing?
str59: For box breathing, breathe in for 4 seconds, hold for 4, breathe out for 4 and hold for 4. For the 4-7-8 technique, breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds, hold for 7, then breathe out through slightly parted lips over 8 seconds. Do the holds without straining; if you have serious heart or lung disease, ask your doctor before using techniques with breath holds.
str60: What are the five skills in the World Health Organization’s stress guide?
str61: Grounding yourself, unhooking from difficult thoughts, acting on your values, being kind to yourself and making room for feelings. The aim is not to make stress disappear completely, but to be able to turn back to what matters to you even when difficult feelings are there.

str71: When should you seek support? If stress, anxiety or low mood has been affecting your sleep, work or relationships for weeks, see a doctor or a mental health professional. If you have thoughts of harming yourself, call 112 straight away.
